lessons.man: Define or display aliases.
lessons.what: Creates a nickname for a long command.
lessons.when: You type 'ls -lah' 50 times a day. Make it two letters.
lessons.tip: Put aliases in ~/.bashrc to keep them forever.

lessons.man: Remove each NAME from the list of defined aliases.
lessons.what: Deletes an alias you created.
lessons.when: That 'funny' alias you made is now confusing you.
lessons.tip: -a removes ALL aliases in the current shell.

lessons.man: Set export attribute for shell variables.
lessons.what: Makes a variable available to programs you run from the shell.
lessons.when: A program needs an API key or setting passed in as a variable.
lessons.tip: Adding to PATH lets you run your own scripts from anywhere.

lessons.man: run a program in a modified environment
lessons.what: Lists all environment variables, or runs a program with changed ones.
lessons.when: Debugging: 'Which settings does my program actually see?'
lessons.tip: VAR=value cmd changes it for that one command only.

lessons.man: Execute commands from a file in the current shell.
lessons.what: Runs a file's commands in your current shell, applying changes instantly.
lessons.when: You edited ~/.bashrc. Apply it without closing the terminal.
lessons.tip: A single dot works too: . ~/.bashrc

quiz.q: Where do you save aliases permanently?
quiz.why: bash reads ~/.bashrc on every new terminal.

quiz.q: Why add a folder to PATH?
options: To run its programs from anywhere
quiz.why: The shell searches PATH for commands.

quiz.q: env LANG=C date changes LANG for...
quiz.why: env sets it just for the program it runs.

lessons.man: make links between files
lessons.what: Creates a shortcut (link) to a file or folder.
lessons.when: Reach a deeply buried folder from your home directory in one step.
lessons.tip: -s makes a symbolic (soft) link, like a desktop shortcut.

lessons.man: print resolved symbolic links or canonical file names
lessons.what: Shows where a link actually points.
lessons.when: That shortcut leads... where exactly?
lessons.tip: -f follows links all the way to the final file.

lessons.man: strip last component from file name
lessons.what: Gives you the folder part of a path (opposite of basename).
lessons.when: In scripts: 'Which folder is this file in?'
lessons.tip: basename = file part, dirname = folder part.

lessons.man: split a file into pieces
lessons.what: Cuts a big file into smaller pieces.
lessons.when: Email allows only 25 MB but your file is 70 MB.
lessons.tip: cat glues the pieces back together.

lessons.man: shrink or extend the size of a file to the specified size
lessons.what: Sets a file to an exact size: empty it, or grow it.
lessons.when: A log file grew to 2 GB. Empty it without deleting it.
lessons.tip: -s 0 empties a file but keeps it in place.

options: Follows links to the final file
quiz.why: -f resolves every link in the chain.

quiz.q: How do you rejoin split pieces?

lessons.man: compute and check MD5 message digest
lessons.what: Creates a short 'fingerprint' of a file.
lessons.when: Did your file get corrupted while copying? Compare fingerprints.
lessons.tip: Change 1 byte and the fingerprint changes completely.

lessons.man: compute and check SHA256 message digest
lessons.what: A stronger fingerprint, used to verify downloads.
lessons.when: Downloading an Ubuntu ISO: is it the real one, untouched?
lessons.tip: -c checks files against a list of known sums.

lessons.man: base64 encode/decode data and print to standard output
lessons.what: Converts data into plain safe text, and back.
lessons.when: Sending binary data through something that only accepts text.
lessons.tip: It's encoding, NOT encryption. Anyone can decode it.

lessons.man: dump files in octal and other formats
lessons.what: Shows the raw bytes inside a file.
lessons.when: Finding invisible characters (like tabs vs spaces) that break things.
lessons.tip: -c shows characters; \n is the newline.

lessons.man: print the sequences of printable characters in files
lessons.what: Pulls readable text out of binary files.
lessons.when: Curious what messages are hidden inside a program file?
lessons.tip: A favourite tool in CTF / cybersecurity challenges.

quiz.why: A hash identifies the exact content.

lessons.man: send ICMP ECHO_REQUEST to network hosts
lessons.what: Checks if another computer or website is reachable.
lessons.when: Wi-Fi is 'connected' but nothing loads. Is the internet alive?
lessons.tip: -c sets how many pings. Without it, Ctrl + C stops.

lessons.man: show / manipulate routing, network devices, interfaces and tunnels
lessons.what: Shows your network interfaces and IP addresses.
lessons.when: Your friend asks 'what's your IP?' to share files on the same Wi-Fi.
lessons.tip: -br = brief output. ip r shows your router (gateway).

lessons.man: another utility to investigate sockets
lessons.what: Shows network connections and which ports are open.
lessons.when: 'Port 3000 already in use.' By whom?
lessons.tip: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -p process, -n numbers.

lessons.man: DNS lookup utility
lessons.what: Looks up the IP address behind a website name.
lessons.when: A site won't open. Is the name even resolving?
lessons.tip: +short gives just the answer. (Package: dnsutils)

lessons.man: transfer a URL
lessons.what: Talks to websites and APIs from the terminal.
lessons.when: Testing an API for your college project without a browser.
lessons.tip: -I headers only, -O save file, -L follow redirects.

quiz.q: Which command shows your IP address?

lessons.man: The non-interactive network downloader.
lessons.what: Downloads files from the internet.
lessons.when: Downloading a big dataset straight into your project folder.
lessons.tip: -c continues a broken download. Lifesaver on bad Wi-Fi.

lessons.man: OpenSSH remote login client
lessons.what: Logs into another computer securely over the network.
lessons.when: Working on your college lab server from your hostel room.
lessons.tip: exit (or Ctrl + D) brings you back home.

lessons.man: OpenSSH secure file copy
lessons.what: Copies files between computers over SSH.
lessons.when: Sending your assignment to the lab server, or fetching results back.
lessons.tip: The . at the end means 'here'.

lessons.man: a fast, versatile, remote (and local) file-copying tool
lessons.what: Smart copy that only transfers what changed.
lessons.when: Backing up your whole project folder every day, quickly.
lessons.tip: Second run? Only changed files are copied.

lessons.man: OpenSSH authentication key utility
lessons.what: Creates a key pair so you can log in without typing passwords.
lessons.when: Tired of typing your password for every ssh and git push.
lessons.tip: Share the .pub key. NEVER share the private one.

quiz.q: How do you leave an ssh session?
In scp file user@host:~/ the file goes...
rsync is faster on repeat runs because...
Which key is safe to share?
